question: Which statements correctly describe conductance?
success: Correct. For a uniform connection, $C=Kwb/L$. Conductance has units of m²/s; multiplying it by a head difference gives discharge. Hydraulic conductivity $K$ describes the material, whereas conductance also includes geometry.
failure: For a uniform connection, $C=Kwb/L$. Conductance has units of m²/s; multiplying it by a head difference gives discharge. Hydraulic conductivity $K$ describes the material, whereas conductance also includes geometry.

question: The width of a uniform connection doubles. Conductivity, saturated thickness, length, and head difference stay unchanged. What follows?
success: Correct. The vertical flow area is $A_\perp=wb$. Doubling width doubles area, conductance, and discharge at the same gradient; it leaves hydraulic conductivity unchanged.
failure: The vertical flow area is $A_\perp=wb$. Doubling width doubles area, conductance, and discharge at the same gradient; it leaves hydraulic conductivity unchanged.

question: Why does the three-cell model combine the resistances of two half-cells?
success: Correct. The two half-cells are connected in series, so their resistances add. Both contribute; a large resistance can dominate. This gives harmonic transmissivity averaging for the three-cell discretization.
failure: The two half-cells are connected in series, so their resistances add. Both contribute; a large resistance can dominate. This gives harmonic transmissivity averaging for the three-cell discretization.
